title: Google Photos: Memory Trail
subtitle: Product Discovery · AI-Native MVP
blurb: Analysed 10,641 public documents, 31 survey responses and six interviews to design an AI-assisted recovery flow for failed photo searches.
overview: Users often remember a moment but not its date, place or details, and stall when the first search fails. Using public-review analysis, a 31-response survey, six task-based interviews and live retrieval replays, I framed the core problem as recovery after a failed first search, then designed Memory Trail: an AI-native concept that keeps clues and near-matches so users narrow results without starting over. In a three-user seeded test, all three recovered their target after the first attempt failed; this is directional evidence, not proof of improved retrieval in real libraries.
highlights: 10,641 public documents analysed for retrieval-friction patterns
31 survey responses and six task-based interviews
3/3 users recovered their target in a seeded test (directional evidence only)

title: Blinkit: Contextual Category Discovery
subtitle: Product Strategy · Growth & Experimentation
blurb: Analysed 3,098+ customer conversations and proposed a contextual add-on to nudge shoppers into new categories without slowing checkout.
overview: Frequent Blinkit shoppers keep buying the same familiar items and rarely explore new categories. I studied the existing discovery surfaces and the friction behind repeat-purchase behaviour, then proposed an AI-powered contextual add-on: it infers the shopper's likely mission from their basket, recommends one relevant item with a clear reason, and lets them accept or ignore it without slowing checkout. The success framework pairs a north-star metric (share of eligible checkouts where a new-category item is bought) with guardrails on checkout time, cart abandonment and relevance.
highlights: 3,098+ customer conversations analysed; initial hypothesis revised toward contextual discovery
North-star: share of eligible checkouts where a new-category item is bought
Guardrails on checkout time, cart abandonment and relevance

title: Myntra: Wishlist Conversion
subtitle: Product Discovery · AI-Powered Product Development
blurb: Analysed 2,055 public conversations, 20 survey responses and six interviews to design a Wishlist comparison flow called Help Me Choose.
overview: High-intent Myntra shoppers save several products for one need, then stall because the comparison is spread across product pages. I combined an AI analysis of 2,055 public conversations with a 20-person survey and 6 interviews to find the root cause, then proposed Help Me Choose: a Wishlist workspace that resolves a 2–4 item shortlist around the shopper's own priorities, with no discounts. The case study covers prioritization, a metrics hierarchy with guardrails, and an experiment plan; no results are claimed.
highlights: 2,055 public conversations analysed, plus a 20-person survey and 6 interviews
Purchase-conversion, decision-speed and quality guardrails defined
Experiment plan included; no results are claimed

title: Subspace.money
subtitle: Product Teardown · May 2026
blurb: End-to-end teardown of a consumer fintech app: onboarding, payment UX and post-transaction trust failures.
overview: End-to-end teardown of a consumer fintech app — analysed onboarding flow, payment UX, and post-transaction trust failures across the full user journey. Diagnosed UX trust breakdown (blank post-payment screen, unlabelled wallet deduction) and recommended tiered fixes prioritized by sprint capacity before GTM.
highlights: Full user journey audited: onboarding, payment UX, post-transaction states
Trust breakdown found: blank post-payment screen and unlabelled wallet deduction
Fixes tiered by sprint capacity before GTM
